Yes, the protestor may be prosecuted. The ordinance is a content-neutral regulation of conduct that serves a legitimate governmental interest in keeping public parks clean, and it is not aimed at suppressing speech. The protestor’s act of dumping trash was not protected expressive conduct under the First Amendment because it was not inherently communicative and the ordinance’s incidental burden on any expressive message is justified by the city’s interest in preventing litter.  
CONFIDENCE: 95
